In summary, our research is concerned with

online learning, which is the study of sequential decision-making under uncertainty, and in particular with bandit online learning, where the learner can only observe the outcome of its own decisions, but not the outcome of other players.
the online linear optimization (OLO) problem in the stochastic setting, where the objective is to minimize regret.
the problem of online learning with bandit feedback.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the best regret bound in the bandit online linear optimization is O ∗ (√T) against an adaptive adversarial adversary, with high probability.
for online linear optimization with a fixed adversary, the regret bound is O ∗ ( n 3/2), while for an adaptive adversary it is O ∗ √ T.
, in the full-information setting, the high-probabitly regret bound is O ∗ (n 1/2 √ T), while in the bandit (or stochastic) setting it is O ∗(n 3/1/2 T).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the first regret bound for the online linear bandit optimization problem that is high-probability and dimension-independent.
we provide the first regret analysis of an online learning algorithm in the bandit model that holds with high probability against an adversarial sequence of losses.
the regret of our algorithm is at most O ∼ ( √ T) with high probability.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bandit setting can be handled in a very similar fashion to the full-information setting.
, in the bandit case, the high-probabilities bounds obtained in the bandit and full-information settings are essentially the same.
the high-probabilities bounds of [8] can be extended to the bandit setting with little effort.
